ig_caption:
On OPT? When your 2026 W-2 arrives (employers must send it by Feb 1, 2027), check box 4 and box 6.

✔️ Box 4 is Social Security tax withheld (6.2%). Box 6 is Medicare tax withheld (1.45%).
✔️ F-1 students who are still nonresidents for tax (generally under 5 calendar years) are usually exempt from both on OPT wages.
✔️ Example: $40,000 of OPT pay with 7.65% taken in error is $3,060.
✔️ Ask your employer to refund it first. If they won't refund all of it, file Form 843 with Form 8316.

Comment FICA and we'll send you the link, or find it at mfa-advisory.com/international-students

General information, not tax advice.

li_caption:
If you worked on OPT in 2026, your W-2 is due from your employer by February 1, 2027. Before you file, look at two boxes.

Box 4 shows Social Security tax withheld (6.2% of wages). Box 6 shows Medicare tax withheld (1.45%).

The IRS says F-1, J-1 and M-1 students who are nonresident aliens, generally those in the US fewer than 5 calendar years, are exempt from both taxes on wages for work USCIS allows, including practical training.

Example: an OPT graduate earns $40,000 and payroll takes 7.65%. That is $3,060 withheld in error.

What to do:

1. Confirm you were still a nonresident for tax in 2026.
2. Ask the employer to refund the Social Security and Medicare it withheld.
3. If the employer won't refund all of it, file Form 843 with Form 8316.

The exemption does not cover F-2, J-2 or M-2 family members, or students who have become residents for tax.

We prepare the 1040-NR and the Form 843 refund claim for international students.
